Perfect! I've found and read both header files. Now let me compile a comprehensive list of all the ppdev ioctl definitions and related constants.

## PPDEV Ioctl Definitions and Constants

### PPDEV IOCTL Commands (23 total)

Based on `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h`, here are all the ppdev ioctl definitions:

| Number | Ioctl Name | Code | Direction | Data Type | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | PPSETMODE | 0x80 | _IOW | int | Set mode for read/write (e.g. IEEE1284_MODE_EPP) |
| 2 | PPRSTATUS | 0x81 | _IOR | unsigned char | Read status |
| 3 | PPWSTATUS | 0x82 | _IOW | unsigned char | Write status (OBSOLETE) |
| 4 | PPRCONTROL | 0x83 | _IOR | unsigned char | Read/write control |
| 5 | PPWCONTROL | 0x84 | _IOW | unsigned char | Write control |
| 6 | PPFCONTROL | 0x8e | _IOW | struct ppdev_frob_struct | Frob control register |
| 7 | PPRDATA | 0x85 | _IOR | unsigned char | Read data |
| 8 | PPWDATA | 0x86 | _IOW | unsigned char | Write data |
| 9 | PPRECONTROL | 0x87 | _IOR | unsigned char | Read econtrol (OBSOLETE) |
| 10 | PPWECONTROL | 0x88 | _IOW | unsigned char | Write econtrol (OBSOLETE) |
| 11 | PPRFIFO | 0x89 | _IOR | unsigned char | Read FIFO (OBSOLETE) |
| 12 | PPWFIFO | 0x8a | _IOW | unsigned char | Write FIFO (OBSOLETE) |
| 13 | PPCLAIM | 0x8b | _IO | none | Claim the port to start using it |
| 14 | PPRELEASE | 0x8c | _IO | none | Release the port when not using it |
| 15 | PPYIELD | 0x8d | _IO | none | Yield the port (release if another driver waiting, then reclaim) |
| 16 | PPFCONTROL | 0x8e | _IOW | struct ppdev_frob_struct | Frob control register |
| 17 | PPEXCL | 0x8f | _IO | none | Register device exclusively (must be before PPCLAIM) |
| 18 | PPDATADIR | 0x90 | _IOW | int | Data line direction: non-zero for input mode |
| 19 | PPNEGOT | 0x91 | _IOW | int | Negotiate a particular IEEE 1284 mode |
| 20 | PPWCTLONIRQ | 0x92 | _IOW | unsigned char | Set control lines when an interrupt occurs |
| 21 | PPCLRIRQ | 0x93 | _IOR | int | Clear (and return) interrupt count |
| 22 | PPSETPHASE | 0x94 | _IOW | int | Set the IEEE 1284 phase that we're in |
| 23 | PPGETTIME | 0x95 | _IOR | struct timeval | Get port timeout |
| 24 | PPSETTIME | 0x96 | _IOW | struct timeval | Set port timeout |
| 25 | PPGETMODES | 0x97 | _IOR | unsigned int | Get available modes (what hardware can do) |
| 26 | PPGETMODE | 0x98 | _IOR | int | Get the current mode |
| 27 | PPGETPHASE | 0x99 | _IOR | int | Get the current phase |
| 28 | PPGETFLAGS | 0x9a | _IOR | int | Get flags |
| 29 | PPSETFLAGS | 0x9b | _IOW | int | Set flags |

### PPDEV Structure

**ppdev_frob_struct** (from `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h`):
```c
struct ppdev_frob_struct {
    unsigned char mask;
    unsigned char val;
};
```

### PPDEV-Specific Flags

From `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h`:
```c
#define PP_FASTWRITE    (1<<2)      /* Fast write flag */
#define PP_FASTREAD     (1<<3)      /* Fast read flag */
#define PP_W91284PIC    (1<<4)      /* Warp9 w91284pic device flag */
#define PP_FLAGMASK     (PP_FASTWRITE | PP_FASTREAD | PP_W91284PIC)  /* Mask for user-visible flags */
```

### IEEE 1284 Mode Flags

From `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`:
```c
#define IEEE1284_MODE_NIBBLE             0           /* Nibble mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_BYTE               (1<<0)      /* Byte mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_COMPAT             (1<<8)      /* Compatibility mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_BECP               (1<<9)      /* Bounded ECP mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECP                (1<<4)      /* ECP mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPRLE             (IEEE1284_MODE_ECP | (1<<5))  /* ECP with RLE */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPSWE             (1<<10)     /* Software-emulated ECP */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPP                (1<<6)      /* EPP mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSL              (1<<11)     /* EPP 1.7 mode */
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSWE             (1<<12)     /* Software-emulated EPP */
#define IEEE1284_DEVICEID                (1<<2)      /* Device ID flag */
#define IEEE1284_EXT_LINK                (1<<14)     /* Extensibility link flag */
#define IEEE1284_ADDR                    (1<<13)     /* Address operations flag */
#define IEEE1284_DATA                    0           /* Data operations flag */
```

### Parport Control Lines

From `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`:
```c
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_STROBE    0x1   /* Strobe control line */
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_AUTOFD    0x2   /* Auto-feed control line */
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_INIT      0x4   /* Initialize control line */
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_SELECT    0x8   /* Select control line */
```

### Parport Status Lines

From `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`:
```c
#define PARPORT_STATUS_ERROR      0x8   /* Error status flag */
#define PARPORT_STATUS_SELECT     0x10  /* Select status flag */
#define PARPORT_STATUS_PAPEROUT   0x20  /* Paper out status flag */
#define PARPORT_STATUS_ACK        0x40  /* Acknowledge status flag */
#define PARPORT_STATUS_BUSY       0x80  /* Busy status flag */
```

### Parport Hardware Mode Flags

From `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`:
```c
#define PARPORT_MODE_PCSPP      (1<<0)  /* IBM PC registers available */
#define PARPORT_MODE_TRISTATE   (1<<1)  /* Can tristate */
#define PARPORT_MODE_EPP        (1<<2)  /* Hardware EPP */
#define PARPORT_MODE_ECP        (1<<3)  /* Hardware ECP */
#define PARPORT_MODE_COMPAT     (1<<4)  /* Hardware 'printer protocol' */
#define PARPORT_MODE_DMA        (1<<5)  /* Hardware can DMA */
#define PARPORT_MODE_SAFEININT  (1<<6)  /* SPP registers accessible in IRQ */
```

### Parport EPP Flags

From `/usr/include/linux/parport.h`:
```c
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST        (1<<0)  /* Unreliable counts / 32-bit EPP transfers */
#define PARPORT_W91284PIC       (1<<1)  /* Warp9 w91284pic device */
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_16     (1<<2)  /* 16-bit EPP transfers */
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_8      (1<<3)  /* 8-bit EPP transfers */
```

### File Locations

- `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h` - PPDEV ioctl definitions
- `/usr/include/linux/parport.h` - Parport and IEEE1284 constants

These are all the definitions you'll need for your syzkaller syzlang descriptions. Note that the header files mention there are some OBSOLETE ioctls (PPWSTATUS, PPRECONTROL, PPWECONTROL, PPRFIFO, PPWFIFO) which are still defined for backward compatibility but should probably be handled carefully in fuzzing scenarios.
